kpis.intro: All measures are kept in a dedicated _Measures table. Base measures are defined first and reused by the KPIs.
kpis.base_measures:
Gross Sales   = SUM ( Sales[LineAmount] )
Discount      = SUM ( Sales[DiscountAmount] )
COGS          = SUMX ( Sales, Sales[Quantity] * RELATED ( Product[UnitCost] ) )
Invoice Count = DISTINCTCOUNT ( Sales[InvoiceNo] )
Sales Target  = SUM ( 'Sales Target'[TargetAmount] )

items.name: Net Sales
items.definition: Revenue after discounts and returns: invoice line amount minus discount, with returns netted off.
items.dax:
Net Sales = [Gross Sales] - [Discount]
-- Returns are already netted as negative-quantity lines (to be confirmed with ERP team)

items.name: Gross Margin %
items.definition: Net Sales minus cost of goods sold, as a share of Net Sales.
items.dax:
Gross Margin % = DIVIDE ( [Net Sales] - [COGS], [Net Sales] )

GM % Status =
SWITCH ( TRUE (),
    [Gross Margin %] >= 0.22, "Green",
    [Gross Margin %] >= 0.18, "Amber",
    "Red" )

items.name: Target Achievement %
items.definition: Net Sales as a share of the sales target for the same month and store.
items.dax:
Target Achievement % = DIVIDE ( [Net Sales], [Sales Target] )

Target Status =
SWITCH ( TRUE (),
    [Target Achievement %] >= 1.00, "Green",
    [Target Achievement %] >= 0.90, "Amber",
    "Red" )

items.name: Average Bill Value
items.dax: Average Bill Value = DIVIDE ( [Net Sales], [Invoice Count] )

items.name: Like-for-Like Growth %
items.definition: Year-on-year Net Sales growth, counting only stores open more than 12 months.
items.dax:
LFL Growth % =
VAR PeriodEnd = MAX ( Sales[InvoiceDate] )
VAR LFLStores =
    FILTER ( VALUES ( Store[StoreCode] ),
             CALCULATE ( MIN ( Store[OpenDate] ) ) <= EDATE ( PeriodEnd, -12 ) )
VAR CurrentYear = CALCULATE ( [Net Sales], LFLStores )
VAR PriorYear   = CALCULATE ( [Net Sales], LFLStores,
                              DATEADD ( Sales[InvoiceDate], -1, YEAR ) )
RETURN DIVIDE ( CurrentYear - PriorYear, PriorYear )

key_decisions: Sales and Sales Target are related through shared Store and Category tables, so actuals and targets can be compared on the same visual.
Incremental refresh on the invoice-line table to meet the 8:00 AM refresh window.
Dynamic row-level security driven by a user-to-region/store mapping table, covering Regional and Store Managers.
Three report pages delivered as one Power BI app, with a mobile layout for Store Managers.

personas.key_decisions: Set regional targets; reallocate promotion budget
Identify under-performing stores; act on margin leakage
Track own store vs target and peer stores

Grant access through Entra ID security groups, not individual users.

security.source_note: Row-level security is based on the two RLS requirements in the BRD Security & NFR sheet.
security.security_table_description: A User Security table maintained by Sales Ops (SharePoint list), loaded into the model and not related to other tables.

roles.requirement: Regional managers see only their region
Store managers see only their store

security.rls_dax:
-- Role: Region   (table: Store)
Store[Region]
    IN CALCULATETABLE ( VALUES ( 'User Security'[Region] ),
                        'User Security'[UserEmail] = USERPRINCIPALNAME () )

-- Role: Store    (table: Store)
Store[StoreCode]
    IN CALCULATETABLE ( VALUES ( 'User Security'[StoreCode] ),
                        'User Security'[UserEmail] = USERPRINCIPALNAME () )
recommendations: Filters flow from Store to both Sales and Sales Target, so one filter secures both.
Test each role with View as in Power BI Desktop and the service before go-live.
Apply a Confidential sensitivity label and disable export of underlying data for the Store role.

practices: Target from BRD: each page renders in under 5 seconds.
Load only the columns listed in the Table & Column Catalogue; remove unused columns from Sales.

deployment.pipeline: Content is promoted with a Power BI deployment pipeline (Dev → Test → Prod). Data source connections and parameters are set per stage through deployment rules.
governance: Version control: save the report as a Power BI Project (PBIP) in Git, with one branch per sprint.
Ownership: dataset owner is the Xebia lead during delivery, transferred to the FreshMart BI team at handover.
Branding: report theme JSON with primary colour #2E7D32 and the FreshMart logo on every page.
Subscriptions: email subscriptions are configured in Production only.

delivery.intro: Work is split into sprints by priority (Must → Should → Could). Sprint length and the number of sprints depend on team size and are agreed separately, so no durations are given.

All tables in Power Query; relationships; base measures; incremental refresh
